The Rise of Caste Armies in Bihar
The text describes a dark period in Bihar's history from the 1970s to the 1990s, marked by brutal caste-based massacres.
It traces the roots of this violence to post-independence land reform laws, which created a new wealthy middle class among backward castes, challenging the old zamindars.
The rise of Naxalite movements, particularly in southern Bihar, armed landless laborers, leading to a cycle of violence.
